# 1. REMOVED (fixed upstream): CRASH item=1767 2368 2369 2370 2371 2372 2373
#    2377 2378 2384 2735 - the equation solver/grapher cluster (fnEqSolvGraph
#    realSlv/cpxSlv/Draw, fnEqCalc, fn1stDerivEq, fn2ndDerivEq, fnComplexPlot).
#    Upstream 3bd0f13ea "fix crash running cpxSlv/Draw/Calc-f with no equation
#    defined" guards the NULL allFormulae dereference in parseEquation and
#    fnEqSolvGraph. Verified by pinning the lane (UPSTREAM_COMMIT): at 3bd0f13ea^
#    all 11 still crash; at 3bd0f13ea exactly these 11 stop, and the same 11 are
#    absent at 87c70c77a. Removed because the finding is fixed, not because the
#    baseline was noisy.
#
# 2. REMOVED (fixed upstream): CRASH item=994 (fnSolveVar), item=1002 (fnIntVar)
#    and item=1611 (fnStoreConfig "STOCFG"), and ADDED leakscan LEAK item=1611 in
#    their place. All four changes are one commit: upstream 29bbdf017
#    "fix(registers): a reserved variable keeps the type it was declared with"
#    (MR !1664). It deleted an out-of-bounds write in setRegisterDataType():
#      allNamedVariables[regist].header.dataType = dataType;   // regist is a
#                                                              // RESERVED index
#    which wrote past allNamedVariables[] into the pool. fnSolveVar and fnIntVar
#    both resolve their variable through findOrAllocateNamedVariable(), which
#    reads that table, so the corruption is what crashed them - not the
#    dynamicMenuItem sentinel the previous note blamed. That guard
#    (currentDynamicSoftmenu()/dynamicMenuItem bounds, upstream 243ae4648) was
#    already present one commit earlier and did NOT retire the entries.
#    Verified by pinning the lane either side of the fix:
#      29bbdf017^ = 5496afd05   CRASH item=994, CRASH item=1611   gate PASSED
#      29bbdf017                LEAK  item=1611, no CRASH         gate FAILED
#    STOCFG no longer crashes because the OOB write became an error return, and
#    the 840 bytes it had already put in the destination register are now
#    visible: pool=840 gmp=0, identical on all four stack types, so a one-shot
#    allocation and not per-iteration growth. That is the configuration block
#    STOCFG exists to store - the same persistent-state class as the LEAK
#    entries below, not an orphan leak.
#
